clue.text: We hear if politician will accept a picture of conditions in the region

definitions.text: picture of conditions in the region

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the sound of the following word gives the letters

parts.note: if means whether, as in 'ask if it will rain'

indicators.note: will accept means the politician takes the next letter inside

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a politician will agree to an image of local conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' signals a sound-alike of the word for 'if'; 'will accept' means the politician's letters hold the A. The definition is a long descriptive phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather map is a chart showing the meteorological conditions over an area.

clue.text: Run, doctor, please run — he's ill again!

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: R again, the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A frantic plea for a doctor to come quickly to someone who has fallen ill again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun being summoned, but it is a verb, the anagram signal, applied to 'please'; the two runs (R in cricket) sit on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who relapses falls back into sickness after seeming to recover.

clue.text: Images manipulated to provoke prejudice

indicators.note: manipulated means the letters of the word beside it are handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Doctored pictures are used to stir up bigotry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manipulated' rearranges IMAGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is a specific kind of prejudice, discrimination on grounds of age.

clue.text: Contract disease and a fever

parts.note: read as one description of an old illness you might catch, marked by bouts of fever and shivering

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the illness: an old word for a malarial fever with fits of shivering.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is the old name for malaria, a disease marked by recurring fever and chills.

clue.text: Promise son to get treatment for speech defect

indicators.note: to get treatment means the letters are worked on and reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone vows that their boy will receive therapy for a stammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get treatment' rearranges PROMISE SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping the opening sounds of words, named after the Reverend Spooner, is jokingly called a slip or defect of speech.

clue.text: Oil is obtained from this Italian city by the ton

indicators.note: by means set next to, so the ton follows the city

parts.note: Bergamo is a city in Lombardy, northern Italy
T is the abbreviation for ton

explanation.surface: Oil arrives by the tonne from a city in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets T after the city. The definition is a description of the fruit rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The bergamot orange yields an essential oil used to flavour Earl Grey tea and in perfumes.

clue.text: Hard worker has Monday off

indicators.note: off means out of order or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diligent employee takes the day after the weekend as leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like time off work, but it rearranges MONDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a figurative term for an energetic, tireless person.

clue.text: Disease consuming upper class lothario

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: STD is a sexually transmitted disease

explanation.surface: A posh womaniser catches a sexually transmitted infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' puts U inside STD.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is slang for a sexually active, womanising man, like the seducer Lothario.

clue.text: e-retailer causing power shortage

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics, as in E=mc squared
Gap is a clothing retailer

explanation.surface: An online shop leaves the country short of electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e-retailer' reads as an online shop, but split it: E stands for ENERGY and the retailer is GAP, the clothing chain.
explanation.definitionFit: An energy gap is a shortfall between the power supply available and what is needed.

clue.text: African country, for example, attracts money from Japan, Britain and Thailand

parts.note: Y stands for the yen, Japanese currency
P, the British penny, with 'money from' carried over
T stands for the tical, an old Thai currency unit, with 'money from' carried over

explanation.surface: A country attracting investment from three nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money from' carries over to Britain and Thailand: Y (yen), P (penny) and T (tical, the old Thai coinage) follow EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Meet at one, set out at about four

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Friends arrange to meet at one, then leave around four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges MEET AT with I (one). The clue's 'at' before the definition is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Teatime in Britain is the late afternoon, traditionally around four o'clock.

clue.text: Suspicious about newspaper's leaders

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject

indicators.note: leaders means only the leading part of the paper's name is kept

parts.note: the Guardian is the British newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone is wary of the editorials in a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' looks like editorials, but here it keeps the front of GUARDIAN, the newspaper that printed this puzzle: GUARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on guard means being wary and alert to danger, close to suspicious.

clue.text: Mopes about in town

indicators.note: about means around or in a muddle, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sulks around a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges MOPES. EPSOM is a Surrey town home to the Derby horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a market town in Surrey, England, famous for its racecourse.

clue.text: The best party over in Saudi Arabia provides drink

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other
over means turned back, so the party's word is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: The finest celebration in Saudi Arabia is dry, so a fizzy soft drink is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the party word backwards, and 'in' sets it inside the Saudi Arabia abbreviation. Saudi Arabia bans alcohol, which makes the soft drink apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream soda is a sweet vanilla-flavoured carbonated soft drink.

clue.text: Bright spark about to gain source of influence over detective

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so these letters come before the next

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
a lever is a means of exerting influence, as in political leverage
a dick is slang for a private detective

explanation.surface: A clever person is about to gain leverage over a police investigator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places C + LEVER above DICK in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever dick is a British informal term for a know-all, a sarcastic 'bright spark'.

clue.text: Chinese and possibly Japanese support for Christian creed

annotationWithheld.why: Chinese and possibly Japanese support for Christian creed: HAN (Chinese) and ASIAN (possibly Japanese) give HANASIAN, but no clue word supplies the opening AT; 'support for' cannot give it, so the clue appears to be missing a word
annotationWithheld.clue: Chinese and possibly Japanese support for Christian creed

clue.text: Actress initially motivated woman to get thin and wealthy

indicators.note: initially means take just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: Arlene is a woman's name
to diet is to try to get thinner
wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: A woman is driven to become slim and well off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letter of 'motivated'. The actress was a German-born Hollywood star of the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a German-American film actress and singer.

clue.text: Achieve position finally in firm

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of each of the two words

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

explanation.surface: Someone at last secures a post at a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E and N, the last letters of 'Achieve' and 'position'. 'firm' looks like a company but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and enduring both describe something lasting, steadfast and not giving way.

clue.text: To this extent Harry is no chum

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so these letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Harry is no friend to this degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a man's name, but it is the verb meaning harass, rearranging IS NO CHUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomuch is an old-fashioned word meaning to such a degree or inasmuch.

clue.text: Churchwarden, perhaps, acquires ideal castle in Spain

parts.note: a churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay pipe, perhaps signalling an example
an ideal is a dream, something hoped for

explanation.surface: A church official takes on an ideal Spanish castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Churchwarden' looks like a church officer but is a long clay tobacco pipe. 'Castle in Spain' is an idiom for a daydream.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle in Spain is an idiom for an unrealistic hope, a fanciful plan never realised.

clue.text: Fine, if in some pain, after exercise

indicators.note: after means the first piece follows the second

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
achy means suffering mild pain

explanation.surface: You feel fine, even if a little sore, after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the pain word behind the exercise abbreviation, physical education at British schools. 'if' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Peachy is informal for excellent or fine, as in 'everything is peachy'.

clue.text: Animal almost extinct twice over

parts.note: describes a beast hunted nearly to extinction whose Latin species name repeats its genus word

explanation.walkthrough: The American beast was nearly wiped out; its scientific name repeats the same word for genus and species, hence 'twice over'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bison is a large wild ox, once near extinction, scientifically named Bison bison.

clue.text: By restricting sexual activity, church appears unkind

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so these letters are placed inside

parts.note: it is a euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: Restricting sex, the church looks mean-spirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' means the first word holds the other two pieces; 'it' is a coy word for sex. 'appears' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitchy means spiteful and malicious, an informal word for unkind.

clue.text: Pole and Russian once had a fight

parts.note: a spar is a pole, as on a ship's mast
Red described a Soviet communist

explanation.surface: A Pole and a Russian once came to blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality, but it is a spar. Red was a nickname for a Soviet.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or argue, so sparred means fought or exchanged blows.

clue.text: Try to escape from constabulary

indicators.note: to escape from means the letters come out of the longer word

explanation.surface: Attempt to break out of police custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to escape from' takes the letters out of CONSTABULARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab means an attempt, as in 'have a stab at it'.

clue.text: Starts to buy evening paper on occasion

indicators.note: Starts to means take the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper

explanation.surface: On some days someone buys an evening newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' takes B and E from 'buy' and 'evening', then the Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Betimes can mean at times or occasionally, as well as early.

clue.text: British convict involved in robbery

parts.note: a lag is a convict, as in 'old lag'

explanation.surface: A British prisoner is caught up in a heist.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG is British slang for a convict. 'involved in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A blag is British slang for a robbery, especially a violent one.

clue.text: Pallid and wooden

definitions.meaning: pallid means pale, drained of colour
wooden means made of ash-tree timber

explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means grey and pale, and also made from the wood of the ash tree.

clue.text: I changed twice for a fashionable tea dance

indicators.note: twice means the same vowel swap is made a second time in the word
changed ... for means the first vowel named is replaced by the second one

parts.note: chichi means showily fashionable
the letter I as written
the letter A as written
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A trendy afternoon tea dance where someone keeps changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' swaps an I for an A in the fashionable word, and 'twice' says to do it to both of its Is. Cha is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance.
